study: How major UK mortgage lenders treat CCJs registered against a limited company where the director's personal credit file is clean
method: Manual browser collection from public intermediary lending-criteria pages. Scripted fetching is blocked by most lender sites. Each row quotes the lender's own published wording.

lenders.trigger: Self-employed applicant with a CCJ or default registered against their business
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: No distinction stated for the business-CCJ trigger. For bankruptcy/IVA/DMP, Halifax does distinguish: over 6 years old AND no longer outstanding can be answered 'No'.
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Wording sits in the general Adverse Credit criteria
lenders.outcome: Disclosure question, then manual assessment. 'CCJs are generally taken into account in credit scoring however background details are required.' Not an automatic decline.
lenders.verbatim: The Credit History question should be answered as 'Yes' if any customer has had a County Court Judgement (CCJ) or default registered against them, or if self employed against their business, within the last 6 years. CCJs are generally taken into account in credit scoring however background details are required.
lenders.source_note: Criteria page, 'Adverse Credit' accordion under General lending criteria
lenders.maintenance_flag: Halifax intermediary brand is migrating to Lloyds. Site notice on the criteria page: 'The Halifax brand is changing to Lloyds.' Expect the URL and possibly the wording to move.

lenders.trigger: Limited company in which the applicant holds greater than 15% shareholding has outstanding judgments totalling more than GBP 5,000
lenders.value_threshold: More than GBP 5,000, outstanding judgments in total
lenders.lookback: None stated for the company-judgment trigger (the 3-year window applies to the applicant's own satisfied CCJs)
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Yes. The trigger is 'outstanding' judgments. Applications can still be considered where documentary evidence of a settled dispute is provided.
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Appears in BOTH books in near-identical wording. The residential book punctuates the clause and writes GBP 5,000; this buy-to-let book writes GBP 5000.
lenders.outcome: Automatic decline trigger. It sits in the 'Adverse credit as detailed below must be declined' list, with a documentary-evidence exception.
lenders.verbatim: If it is identified that a Limited Company in which an applicant has greater than 15% shareholding has any outstanding judgements totalling more than GBP 5000 ... Applications can be considered where the above is identified but only where documentary evidence of a settled dispute has been provided by the customer.

lenders.trigger: Limited company in which the applicant holds greater than 15% shareholding has outstanding judgments totalling more than GBP 5,000
lenders.value_threshold: More than GBP 5,000, outstanding judgments in total
lenders.lookback: None stated for the company-judgment trigger
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Yes. Trigger is 'outstanding'. Documentary evidence of a settled dispute can rescue the application.
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Residential. The same criterion appears in the buy-to-let book in near-identical wording (punctuation differs, and the buy-to-let book writes GBP 5000 rather than GBP 5,000).
lenders.outcome: Automatic decline trigger, in the 'must be declined' list, with a documentary-evidence exception.
lenders.verbatim: If it is identified that a limited company, in which an applicant has greater than 15% shareholding, has any outstanding judgements totaling more than GBP 5,000 ... Applications can be considered where the above is identified but only where documentary evidence of a settled dispute has been provided by the customer.
lenders.correction_flag: RESOLVED 12 Aug 2026. /county-court-judgements/ previously said the Barclays rule was 'a buy-to-let rule, not a residential one'. That was wrong and has been corrected. Do not reintroduce it.
lenders.reverification: Re-verified 12 Aug 2026 after reviewer challenge. On the residential URL the rule sits 658 characters after the heading "Adverse credit history - Residential", inside the "must be declined" list, with no buy-to-let wording within the preceding 2,500 characters. The residential claim is sound.
lenders.personal_ccj_threshold_note: Barclays personal satisfied-CCJ limit is GBP 200, the strictest in the sample, against a company-judgment threshold of GBP 5,000.

lenders.trigger: Published CCJ criteria address the applicant's own judgments only
lenders.value_threshold: None published, though value is said to matter
lenders.lookback: None published, though date registered is said to matter
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Not distinguished in the published wording ('current or previous CCJs')
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Residential. Buy-to-let sits with The Mortgage Works, listed separately.
lenders.outcome: Case-by-case underwriting on the applicant's own CCJs. Nothing published about company judgments.
lenders.verbatim: County Court Judgements (CCJ): We'll consider lending to applicants that have current or previous CCJs depending on the value and the date registered.

lenders.trigger: Application question asks about a judgment 'against them', meaning the applicant personally
lenders.value_threshold: None published. No minimum value, so any personal CCJ counts.
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Not distinguished. The question covers any CCJ in the last 6 years.
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Stated in the general Adverse Credit criteria
lenders.outcome: Automatic decline on a personal CCJ. Nothing published about company judgments.
lenders.verbatim: Within the application we ask: In the last 6 years has your client(s) had a debt repayment plan with creditors, been declared bankrupt or had a county court judgement against them? If the answer is 'yes' to this question, we are unable to accept the application.
lenders.note: The strictest personal-CCJ rule in the sample, yet no company-judgment question is published.

lenders.trigger: No CCJ question appears in the published eligibility questions at all
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Residential criteria checked. Buy-to-let is a separate criteria set.
lenders.outcome: Handled inside credit scoring rather than a published rule. 'Some adverse credit history' is listed as a marker of a low credit score, and low-scoring applications may be declined.
lenders.verbatim: Eligibility questions ... Also, has any client on the application: Ever had a property repossessed by a mortgage lender? Ever been bankrupt or subject to an IVA? Ever had a criminal conviction ... (no CCJ question)

lenders.trigger: Uses the FCA 'credit impaired' definition, which is framed around the applicant as an individual
lenders.value_threshold: More than GBP 500 total, applicant's own judgments
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Not distinguished. The test is total value within 3 years.
lenders.outcome: Automatic decline where the applicant meets the credit-impaired definition. Nothing published about company judgments.
lenders.verbatim: The bank will not consider applications from applicants that are defined by the FCA as Credit Impaired as follows: ... Has been the subject of one or more county court judgments, with a total value greater than GBP500, within the last three years.

lenders.value_threshold: None. Zero CCJs permitted in the window.
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Yes. All CCJs must be satisfied, and none may be registered in the last 6 years.
lenders.outcome: Policy decline, but Accord publishes a 'common-sense lending' route for cases outside policy.
lenders.verbatim: CCJ: All CCJs must be satisfied. 0 registered in the last 6 years. ... Common-sense lending: We will consider cases that are outside of our lending policy in this area if you get in touch.

lenders.trigger: Applicant's own CCJs and defaults, combined value
lenders.shareholding_threshold: None published for judgments. Shareholding thresholds exist, but only for who must be assessed and guarantee.
lenders.value_threshold: GBP 100 or less usually considered. Up to GBP 500 may be considered. More than GBP 500 generally not accepted.
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Not distinguished. Wording covers 'current or historic' CCJs.
lenders.outcome: Value-banded. Low values considered, higher values generally declined.
lenders.verbatim: Applicants with current or historic CCJs and/or Defaults may be considered where the combined value is GBP 100 or less. We may also consider applications where the combined value of CCJs and/or Defaults is up to GBP 500 ... In general, we will not accept applicants who, within the last six years, have had: CCJs and/or Defaults with a combined value more than GBP 500.
lenders.note: Notable: TMW is a limited-company buy-to-let specialist and its dedicated Limited Company criteria page still publishes no company-judgment rule. Minority shareholders are explicitly not credit assessed.

lenders.value_threshold: Satisfied CCJs, maximum GBP 500. Unsatisfied CCJs of any value are unacceptable.
lenders.lookback: 6 years, plus a 6-month exclusion window for recently registered satisfied CCJs
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Yes, sharply. Unsatisfied CCJs of any value are not accepted. Satisfied CCJs are allowed within limits.
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Residential policy page. Buy-to-let criteria are separate.
lenders.outcome: Policy limits, applied as decline thresholds. Cases over 85% LTV may be assessed individually.
lenders.verbatim: CCJs: Unsatisfied - no CCJs of any value that are currently unsatisfied. Satisfied - no CCJs registered in the last 6 months. In the last 6 years, maximum 1 satisfied CCJ and the value must be no more than GBP 500.

lenders.trigger: Applicant's own CCJs, expressly as they appear on the credit report
lenders.value_threshold: Total value of all CCJs on the credit report must be less than GBP 500
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Yes. All CCJs must be satisfied at the time of application.
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Residential A-Z. A separate buy-to-let A-Z exists.
lenders.outcome: Acceptable within limits, subject to the overall credit score.
lenders.verbatim: County/High Court Judgements ... 1 CCJ registered in last 3 years. Total value of all CCJs on the credit report must be less than GBP 500. All CCJs must be satisfied at the time of application.
lenders.note: The phrase 'on the credit report' matters. A company's CCJ is not on the director's personal credit report, so it falls outside this test by definition.

lenders.trigger: Applicant's own CCJs only, via a published credit history matrix
lenders.value_threshold: Combined CCJs under GBP 500 satisfied, or under GBP 250 unsatisfied, for judgments 6 months to 3 years old
lenders.lookback: None in the last 6 months. Over 3 years old, considered individually.
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Yes. Separate and lower limits for unsatisfied judgments.
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Residential criteria. Buy-to-let and limited company buy-to-let criteria are published separately.
lenders.outcome: Matrix limits, with individual consideration for older judgments and an appeals route.
lenders.verbatim: We will consider applications from applicants with previous CCJs, defaults or arrears, provided they do not exceed the limits in the Credit history matrix. ... CCJs over 6 months up to 3 years: If the combined total value of CCJs is less than GBP 500 satisfied, or the combined total value of CCJs is less than GBP 250 unsatisfied.

lenders.trigger: Applicant's business, where the applicant is self-employed
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Not distinguished for the business-CCJ trigger
lenders.outcome: Disclosure question feeding credit scoring, plus manual background detail. Not an automatic decline.
lenders.verbatim: Please answer 'Yes' to the credit history question if any customer has had a County Court Judgement (CCJ) or default registered against them, or their business if they're self-employed, within the last six years. CCJs are generally considered in credit scoring. Background details will be need for the application.

lenders.trigger: Any director or shareholder, or their business where self-employed
lenders.shareholding_threshold: None. The question covers any director or shareholder, with no minimum stake.
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Not distinguished for the business-CCJ trigger
lenders.outcome: Disclosure question feeding credit scoring, plus manual background detail.
lenders.verbatim: Please answer 'Yes' to the credit history question if any directors or shareholders have had a County Court Judgement (CCJ) or default registered against them, or their business if they're self-employed, within the last six years.
lenders.note: This is the widest company-CCJ question found. It reaches any director or shareholder, with no shareholding floor and no value floor.

lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Yes. Unsatisfied CCJs are not acceptable at all.
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Single criteria document covering residential and buy-to-let
lenders.outcome: Policy limits, applied as decline thresholds.
lenders.verbatim: County Court Judgements and Defaults: Maximum of one County Court Judgement (CCJ) or default satisfied in the last 3 years which must have been satisfied and be no greater than GBP 500 in value will be considered. Unsatisfied County Court Judgements and defaults are not acceptable.
lenders.source_note: Mortgage Lending Criteria and Guidance, the document's own effective date is 6 August 2026
lenders.note: The document has a section on directors of limited companies, but only for income assessment. It says nothing about judgments against the company.

lenders.value_threshold: None. Zero CCJs permitted in the window.
lenders.satisfied_vs_outstanding: Not distinguished in the allowable-adverse table
lenders.residential_vs_btl: Buy-to-let criteria guide, covering both individual and limited company applicants
lenders.outcome: Policy limit on the applicant's own record.
lenders.verbatim: Allowable adverse: Defaults 0 in 24 months. CCJs 0 in 24 months.
lenders.source_note: Criteria guide, buy to let mortgages, version 77. The document states 'Correct as of: 22 May 2023'.
lenders.staleness_warning: The published document carries a 2023 date. Treat this row as weaker evidence than the others and re-check against a current Precise criteria source before relying on it.

pattern_findings.who_asks: Three brands ask about company judgments, and they belong to two banking groups. Halifax and BM Solutions are both Lloyds Banking Group and share near-identical wording. Barclays asks in both its residential and its buy-to-let books.
pattern_findings.who_is_silent: Eleven of the fourteen publish no company-judgment criterion. That is an absence of a published rule, not evidence that those lenders never ask. Their published CCJ rules are written around the applicant's personal credit record, and underwriting discretion sits behind every published criterion.
pattern_findings.where_thresholds_cluster: Personal CCJ value limits cluster tightly at GBP 500. HSBC, Virgin Money, Skipton, Coventry, Leeds and The Mortgage Works all use GBP 500 or lower. Look-back windows cluster at 3 years and 6 years. The only company-judgment value threshold found is Barclays at GBP 5,000, ten times the common personal limit.
pattern_findings.shareholding: Only Barclays sets a shareholding floor, at more than 15%. The Lloyds group question has no shareholding floor at all but is tied to the applicant being self-employed.
pattern_findings.decline_versus_disclose: The two approaches are genuinely different. Barclays treats a qualifying company judgment as a decline trigger, escapable only with documentary evidence of a settled dispute. Lloyds group treats it as a disclosure question feeding credit scoring and manual review.
pattern_findings.satisfied_versus_outstanding: Barclays keys its company rule to outstanding judgments, so satisfying the judgment moves the case. The Lloyds group question does not distinguish, so a satisfied company CCJ still has to be declared.
pattern_findings.residential_versus_btl: The split is not as clean as commonly assumed. Barclays carries the same company-judgment criterion in both books in near-identical wording. Lloyds group asks in residential (Halifax) and in buy-to-let (BM Solutions), including its limited company range.

evidence_caveat: Rows marked 'No published criterion' record what we could not find in published intermediary criteria. Absence of a published rule is not proof that a lender will never ask about company judgments in an application, in underwriting, or on a case-specific referral. Do not report these rows as 'the lender does not ask'.
